vocabulary.meaning: a strong-smelling bulb used as a food and seasoning
examples: Garlic is common in many cuisines.
She added fresh garlic to the sauce.

vocabulary.meaning: one of the small sections that make up a bulb of garlic
examples: The recipe uses two cloves of garlic.
Crush the garlic clove before adding it.

vocabulary.meaning: having a strong, sharp smell or taste
examples: Raw garlic has a pungent flavour.
Cooking makes the pungent taste milder.

vocabulary.meaning: a noticeable and often pleasant smell
examples: The aroma of garlic filled the kitchen.
Roasted garlic has a sweeter aroma.
Some people eat small amounts of raw garlic.
Raw garlic tastes stronger than cooked garlic.

vocabulary.meaning: to cook food using dry heat, usually in an oven
examples: Roast the garlic until it becomes soft.
Roasted garlic spreads easily on bread.

vocabulary.meaning: one of the substances used to make a dish
examples: Garlic is a key ingredient in the recipe.
Check the ingredient list if you dislike garlic.

vocabulary.meaning: something added to food to improve flavour
examples: Garlic is often used as a seasoning.
Herbs and garlic can reduce the need for extra salt.

vocabulary.meaning: a positive effect something may have on health
examples: Researchers study possible health benefits of garlic.
A single food should not be treated as a cure, even if it has health benefits.

vocabulary.meaning: an unpleasant smell on the breath after eating garlic
examples: He joked about his garlic breath after lunch.
Parsley does not always remove garlic breath.
